lanes: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: Heliopolitan solar theology
spans.note: The solar cult of the Old Kingdom, before the earliest inscribed Pyramid Texts.

spans.label: Pyramid Texts
spans.note: Inscribed in the pyramid of Unas and his Sixth Dynasty successors at Saqqara.

spans.label: Coffin Texts
spans.note: Middle Kingdom coffins, above all from Deir el-Bersha and Asyut.

spans.label: Great Hymn to the Aten
spans.note: Akhenaten’s reign; the hymn is inscribed in the tomb of Ay at Akhetaten.

spans.label: Litany of Re
spans.note: Earliest copies in the tombs of Useramun and Thutmose III in the Valley of the Kings.

spans.label: Amduat
spans.note: The earliest complete version is in the tomb of Thutmose III; the composition is somewhat older.

spans.label: Book of Gates
spans.note: First in the tomb of Horemheb; complete on the alabaster sarcophagus of Seti I.

spans.label: Book of Caverns
spans.note: From the Osireion at Abydos under Merenptah to the full version in the tomb of Ramesses VI.

spans.label: Book of the Heavenly Cow
spans.note: First on the outermost shrine of Tutankhamun; fully in the tombs of Seti I and Ramesses II, III, and VI.

spans.label: Akh and the transfigured dead
spans.note: From the Pyramid Texts through the funerary literature of the Late Period.

spans.label: Utu-Shamash, the all-seeing
spans.note: From the Ur III hymns to Utu to the Neo-Assyrian copies of the Great Hymn to Šamaš; Sippar and Larsa were his cult cities.

spans.label: Light, justice, and divine vision
spans.note: The stele of Hammurabi (c. 1755 BCE) shows Šamaš conferring the measures of justice; the Great Hymn makes the sun the judge who sees all.

spans.label: The Gāthās
spans.note: Usually placed c. 1200–1000 BCE, with proposals from c. 1500 down to c. 600; their homeland is the eastern Iranian world, for which Bactria stands.

spans.label: Avestan fire
spans.note: The Younger Avesta’s fire liturgies (Ātaš Niyāyišn, Yasna 62); the fire temples of Pārs are the later institution.

spans.label: Star, moon, sun, and Endless Light
spans.note: The ascent by stations of the Younger Avesta (Hādōxt Nask, Vidēvdād 19).

spans.label: Bundahišn
spans.note: Pahlavi compilation of the ninth century from Sasanian materials, revised into the twelfth.

spans.label: Plato · Republic VI–VII
spans.note: Sun, Divided Line, and Cave; Plato lived c. 428–348 BCE.

spans.label: Aristotle · De anima II.7
spans.note: The doctrine of the transparent (diaphanes); Aristotle lived 384–322 BCE.

spans.label: On Colours
spans.note: Peripatetic, perhaps by Theophrastus or Strato, transmitted under Aristotle’s name.

spans.label: Euclid · Optics
spans.note: Euclid flourished at Alexandria c. 300 BCE.

spans.label: Ptolemy · Optics
spans.note: Ptolemy lived c. 100–170 CE.

spans.label: Stoic and Roman theories of vision
spans.note: Chrysippus (c. 279–206 BCE) to Galen (129–c. 216 CE); Lucretius (c. 99–55 BCE) for the Epicurean films.

spans.label: Phanes and the Orphic theogonies
spans.note: From the theogony read by the Derveni papyrus (poem c. 500 BCE, papyrus c. 340) to the Rhapsodies of the early centuries CE.

spans.label: Chaldean Oracles
spans.note: The two Julians, father and son, under Marcus Aurelius; the oracles’ own geography is unknown, and Rome stands for the court they served.

spans.label: Poimandres (Corpus Hermeticum I)
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: The Eighth and the Ninth
spans.note: Composed in Greek in Roman Egypt; the Coptic copy was buried near Nag Hammadi c. 350.
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: The Hermetic rebirth (CH XIII)
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: Apocryphon of John
spans.note: Known to Irenaeus by c. 180.
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: Pistis Sophia
spans.note: Coptic; the Askew Codex.
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: Books of Jeu
spans.note: Coptic; the Bruce Codex, from Upper Egypt.
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: Mani
spans.note: Mani preached from Seleucia-Ctesiphon and died in the prison of Bahram I.
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: The Kephalaia of the Teacher
spans.note: The five living elements of light in the Coptic Kephalaia found at Medinet Madi.
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: The Manichaean church and its texts
spans.note: From Mani’s death to the Uyghur and Chinese communities whose texts survive from Turfan and Dunhuang.
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: Ginza Rabba
spans.note: The Mandaean scriptures were compiled between the third and seventh centuries in the marshlands of southern Mesopotamia and Khūzistān.
spans.lane: Hermetic, Gnostic, Manichaean, and Mandaean Traditions

spans.label: Genesis 1
spans.note: The Priestly creation account, usually placed in or after the exile.

spans.label: The pillar of fire (Exodus 13–14)
spans.note: The wilderness of Sinai is the narrative’s setting; its composition belongs to the Judahite and exilic centuries.

spans.label: Ezekiel’s throne vision
spans.note: Dated by the book itself; among the exiles by the Chebar canal.

spans.label: Daniel 7
spans.note: The visions of Daniel 7–12 come from the Maccabean crisis.

spans.label: 1 Enoch · the Astronomical Book
spans.note: Aramaic copies were found at Qumran.

spans.label: The hidden light in rabbinic tradition
spans.note: Genesis Rabbah (Galilee, c. 400–450) and the Babylonian Talmud’s Ḥagigah (c. 500).

spans.label: Gospel of John
spans.note: Traditionally Ephesus.

spans.label: The Transfiguration
spans.note: Mark’s account, c. 70 CE; the mountain is unnamed, Tabor is the traditional site, and Hermon the other candidate.

spans.label: Paul · 2 Corinthians 3
spans.note: Written to Corinth from Macedonia.

spans.label: Odes of Solomon
spans.note: Syriac hymns of the second century, usually placed in Edessa or Antioch.

spans.label: Gregory of Nyssa
spans.note: The Life of Moses c. 390.

spans.label: Pseudo-Dionysius
spans.note: The corpus surfaces in Syria around 500 and is first cited at Constantinople in 532.

spans.label: The robe of light in Syriac Christianity
spans.note: From the Hymn of the Pearl in the Acts of Thomas (c. 200–250) to Ephrem (d. 373).

spans.label: The Upaniṣads
spans.note: Bṛhadāraṇyaka and Chāndogya (c. 800–600 BCE) to the middle Upaniṣads.

spans.label: Bhagavad Gītā
spans.note: The battlefield of Kurukṣetra is the poem’s setting; its composition is placed between the second century BCE and the second CE.

spans.label: Tejas in the elemental systems
spans.note: Vaiśeṣika Sūtra and Caraka Saṃhitā to the Sāṃkhya-kārikā; Takṣaśilā and Kāśī were the medical and philosophical centres.

spans.label: Sāṃkhya-kārikā
spans.note: Īśvarakṛṣṇa’s verses, c. 350; where they were composed is not known.

spans.label: Yogic signs of light
spans.note: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 2.11 (c. 400–200 BCE) to Yoga Sūtra 1.36 (c. 350–450 CE).

spans.label: The luminous mind (Aṅguttara Nikāya)
spans.note: Transmitted orally before being written down in Sri Lanka in the first century BCE.

spans.label: Upakkilesa Sutta
spans.note: Set at Pācīnavaṃsa, near Kosambī.

spans.label: Visuddhimagga · the light kasiṇa
spans.note: Buddhaghosa at Anurādhapura, c. 430.

spans.label: Early Mahāyāna radiance
spans.note: The earliest Mahāyāna sūtras (Aṣṭasāhasrikā, Sukhāvatīvyūha); Gandhāra preserves the oldest manuscripts.

spans.label: Tathāgatagarbha sūtras
spans.note: Composed in India from the third century; translated in China in the early fifth, Buddhabhadra’s Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra at Jiankang in 420.

spans.label: Tantric and Tibetan clear light
spans.note: Guhyasamāja (c. 8th century) and the cycle of Nāropa (11th) to Tsongkhapa (d. 1419).

spans.label: The Mohist canons on light and shadow
spans.note: The optical propositions of the Mo jing; Mozi came from Lu.

spans.label: Dao De Jing
spans.note: The Guodian bamboo slips (c. 300 BCE) are the oldest witness.

spans.label: Zhuangzi
spans.note: Zhuang Zhou of Meng, in Song; the Inner Chapters.

spans.label: Neiye
spans.note: Transmitted in the Guanzi of the Jixia academy at Linzi.

spans.label: Yin-yang, sun, and moon
spans.note: Correlative cosmology from Zou Yan to the Huainanzi (139 BCE).

spans.label: Cantong qi
spans.note: Ascribed to Wei Boyang of Kuaiji, 142 CE; the received text took shape over the following centuries.

spans.label: Secret of the Golden Flower
spans.note: The Taiyi jinhua zongzhi emerged in the Jingming milieu of Jiangxi in the late seventeenth century.

spans.label: The Light Verse (Qurʾan 24:35)
spans.note: Sūrat al-Nūr is Medinan.

spans.label: Ibn al-Haytham
spans.note: Kitāb al-Manāẓir, c. 1011–21, at Cairo.

spans.label: al-Ghazālī
spans.note: Mishkāt al-anwār, written in his last years.

spans.label: Suhrawardī
spans.note: Executed at Aleppo.

spans.label: Ḥikmat al-ishrāq
spans.note: Completed in 1186, by its author’s own dating.

spans.label: Illumination in Islamic mysticism
spans.note: From the early Sufis of Baghdad (Junayd, d. 910) through Ibn ʿArabī (d. 1240, Damascus) and Rūmī (d. 1273, Konya) to Mullā Ṣadrā of Shiraz (d. 1640).

spans.label: Robert Grosseteste
spans.note: De luce, c. 1225.

spans.label: Perspectiva
spans.note: Roger Bacon (Opus maius, 1267), Witelo (Perspectiva, c. 1270–78, at Viterbo), John Pecham (c. 1280).

spans.label: Marsilio Ficino
spans.note: De sole, 1494.

spans.label: Jacob Böhme
spans.note: Aurora, 1612.

spans.label: Robert Fludd
spans.note: Utriusque cosmi historia, 1617–21.

spans.label: Isaac Newton
spans.note: Opticks, 1704.

spans.label: Goethe
spans.note: Zur Farbenlehre, 1810.

spans.label: Éliphas Lévi
spans.note: Dogme et rituel de la haute magie, 1854–56.

spans.label: The Golden Dawn
spans.note: From the founding of the Isis-Urania temple to the schisms of 1900–03.

spans.label: Theosophical planes and rays
spans.note: Founded in New York in 1875 and seated at Adyar from 1882; the doctrine of planes and rays runs from The Secret Doctrine (1888) to Alice Bailey’s ray books.

spans.label: Rudolf Steiner
spans.note: The four ethers were set out by Guenther Wachsmuth at Dornach in 1924 from Steiner’s indications.

spans.label: Ancient optical theories
spans.note: Empedocles to Ptolemy.

spans.label: From visual rays to incoming light
spans.note: From Ibn al-Haytham’s Kitāb al-Manāẓir (1011–21) to Kepler’s Paralipomena (Prague, 1604), which completed the reversal.

spans.label: The sine law of refraction
spans.note: Found by Willebrord Snell at Leiden in 1621; published by Descartes in 1637.

spans.label: Fermat’s principle of least time
spans.note: Generalising Hero of Alexandria’s least path for reflection.

spans.label: Newton’s prism
spans.note: The experiments of 1666 and the letter to the Royal Society of 1672.

spans.label: Wave theories of light
spans.note: Huygens’ Traité de la lumière (1690), Young’s interference (1801), Fresnel’s memoir on diffraction (1818).

spans.label: Light as electromagnetism
spans.note: Faraday’s rotation (1845), Maxwell’s equations (1865), Hertz’s waves (1888).

spans.label: The light quantum
spans.note: Planck (1900) and Einstein (1905); Compton’s scattering (1923, St Louis) lies beyond the map.

spans.label: Wave–particle duality
spans.note: De Broglie’s matter waves (1924) and Bohr’s complementarity (1927).

spans.label: Polarization
spans.note: Bartholin’s double refraction (1669) to Malus’s law (1808).

spans.label: Interference and diffraction
spans.note: Grimaldi (1665), Young (1801), Fresnel (1818).

spans.label: Coherence and the laser
spans.note: Basov and Prokhorov in Moscow and Townes in New York proposed the maser in 1954; Maiman’s ruby laser (1960, Malibu) lies beyond the map.

spans.label: Colour temperature
spans.note: Wien’s displacement law (1893) and Planck’s law (1900).

spans.label: Photometry
spans.note: Bouguer’s Essai d’optique (1729) and Lambert’s Photometria (1760).

spans.label: Theories of colour vision
spans.note: Young (1802), Helmholtz (1852–67), Hering (1878).

spans.label: Beyond the visible
spans.note: Herschel’s infrared (1800) and Ritter’s ultraviolet (1801).

spans.label: Spectroscopy of the heavens
spans.note: Fraunhofer’s lines (1814), Kirchhoff and Bunsen (1859), Huggins on the nebulae (1864).

spans.label: Light, space, and relativity
spans.note: Special relativity (Bern, 1905) and general relativity (Berlin, 1915); Eddington’s eclipse of 1919 was observed at Príncipe, beyond the map.

spans.label: The discovery of photosynthesis
spans.note: Priestley (1771) and Ingenhousz (1779).

spans.label: Bioluminescence
spans.note: From Boyle’s finding that glow needs air (1667) to Dubois’s luciferin and luciferase (1885–87).

spans.label: Circadian biology
spans.note: De Mairan’s mimosa (1729) to Bünning’s endogenous clock (1935).

spans.label: Biophotons
spans.note: Gurwitsch’s mitogenetic rays, found at Simferopol in 1923, to Popp’s measurements at Marburg from 1976.

spans.label: Phosphenes and the inner light
spans.note: Purkinje’s studies at Prague (1819–25); Penfield’s cortical stimulation (Montreal, 1937) lies beyond the map.
